_note: Narration script for the Chest pain module (CPP-007-AO v4.2). Generated as one take; one paragraph per scene.

lines.head: Introduction
sentences: Chest pain.
What every Ambulance Officer needs to know.

lines.head: Think cardiac
sentences: There are many causes of chest pain, but suspect cardiac ischaemia unless there is an obvious alternative.
It can feel like pain, pressure, heaviness or tightness in the chest, neck, jaw, arms, back or shoulder, with nausea, dizziness, sweating or shortness of breath.
Time is muscle.

lines.head: First steps
sentences: Start with basic care, including E C G monitoring.
Check vital signs every five minutes, and consider clinical support.
Unless the patient is allergic, give oral aspirin, three hundred milligrams.

lines.head: GTN limits
sentences: G T N is a sublingual dose of three hundred micrograms, and it can drop the blood pressure.
So check first.
For a patient with G T N prescribed, the systolic pressure must be at least one hundred, the pulse between sixty and one hundred and twenty, and there must be no recent P D E five inhibitor.

lines.head: PDE-5 inhibitors
sentences: No G T N within twenty four hours of sildenafil, vardenafil or avanafil, or within forty eight hours of tadalafil.
Together they can cause life threatening low blood pressure.

lines.head: GTN prescribed
sentences: If G T N is prescribed and the limits are met, give one dose.
Monitor vital signs every three to five minutes.
If the pain persists and the limits still hold, repeat every five minutes as needed, to a maximum of three doses.

lines.head: GTN not prescribed
sentences: If G T N has not been prescribed, consult the E O C Clinician, who may advise it.
The same limits apply, but the systolic pressure must be above one hundred.

lines.head: Call the EOC
sentences: Consult the E O C Clinician if blood pressure or heart rate fall outside the limits at any time.
Or if the pain is not resolved.
Or if pain that had gone away comes back.

lines.head: Checks and transport
sentences: Do the medication checks, with a second clinician whenever possible.
Provide transport, and notify the receiving facility.

lines.head: Wrap-up
sentences: So: think cardiac, give aspirin unless allergic, check the pressure, pulse and P D E five before G T N, and stop at three doses.
Call the E O C Clinician if anything changes.
Now try the G T N checker on this page.
